newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices mixed, volume increases.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices mixed, volume increases.

text.p: Gold prices ended mixed on Istanbul's gold exchange on Thursday as increased free market demand boosted volume, dealers said.
Gold closed at $382.50 an ounce, down from Wednesday's $383.75 in line with the falls in Europe.

But it rose to 1,122,500 lira per gram from a previous 1,119,400 lira due to the lira's weakness. The lira ended at 91,250 to the dollar versus 90,720 on Wednesday as the dollar gained against the mark in international markets.
Traded volume nearly tripled to 963 kilos from 364.

"Demand was firm in the morning because gold prices in the free market were higher than those on the bourse. But the lira eased against the dollar in the interbank later in the day, increasing (gold) prices of seller banks," said one dealer.
"Falling gold prices in world markets also caused demand to diminish in the second session," he added.
Volume dived to 189 kilos in the second session from 774 in the morning.
There was no dollar term trade in the afternoon, and 79.8 percent of daily turnover was in lira terms.
